# Ledger: operations guide

Version 1.0.0 of the specification: 0 monitors, 0 jobs, 0 dependencies and 0 endpoints. For the people who run the live system: where it runs, what to look at each day, what to do when a monitor's objective is missed, what runs on its own, what it depends on, and how its data is saved and brought back.

## 1. Where it runs

The specification has no environments; each place the system runs, and the one a release is promoted to next, is written under environments.

## 2. Daily checklist

The specification has no monitors, jobs or dependencies, so there is nothing to look at each day; they are written under monitors, jobs and dependencies.

## 3. Monitors

The specification has no monitors; what is watched on the live system, and the objective it must meet, is written under monitors.

## 4. Jobs

The specification has no jobs; what the system runs on its own, on a schedule or for each message, is written under jobs.

## 5. Channels

The specification has no channels; the messages the system publishes and consumes are written under channels.

## 6. Dependencies

The specification has no dependencies; each system it calls or that carries its channels is written under dependencies.

## 7. Endpoints

The specification has no endpoints; each operation the system serves is written under paths.

## 8. Settings

The specification has no settings; each value the system reads at run time is written under configuration.

## 9. Backing up

The specification has no backup; how the data of the live system is saved is written under backup.

## 10. Restoring

The specification has no restore; how saved data is brought back is written under restore.

## 11. Rolling back

The specification has no rollback; how a release is taken back is written under rollback.
